Instagram auto-reply and DM automation for restaurants · Bookline

INSTAGRAM ASSISTANT FOR RESTAURANTS

# Instagram auto-replies that end in a booking

Guests message you on Instagram at all hours: to book, to ask for the menu or to check if there’s a table. Bookline’s assistant answers straight away, turns every comment into a private conversation, and publishes and schedules your posts.

[Request your demo](https://bookline.ai/en/products/instagram-ai#contacto)[How it works](https://bookline.ai/en/products/instagram-ai#como-funciona)

![Person typing a message on their phone at night](/_next/image?url=%2Fimages%2Finstagram-hero-dm.webp&w=3840&q=75)

Official Meta API

Hi! Do you have a table for 2 tonight?

Yes! We have 9:00 pm and 10:00 pm. Which works best?

9:00 pm 🙌

Done: tonight at 9:00 pm, 2 people. See you then!

SOUND FAMILIAR?

## Your Instagram gets questions nobody answers in time

Instagram is where guests find you. But messages arrive mid-service or at midnight, and every one left unanswered is a table that goes somewhere else.

![Person typing a message on their phone on the sofa](/_next/image?url=%2Fimages%2Finstagram-problems-phone.webp&w=3840&q=75)

### Someone asks for a table by DM and you reply the next day

By then they’ve booked somewhere else. On Instagram, whoever doesn’t reply fast loses the booking.

### Comments go unanswered

“Price?”, “Any vegan options?”, “Info”. Every comment is someone interested, and almost nobody replies to them in private.

### The same questions, every day

Opening hours, the menu, how to get there, whether dogs are allowed. Your team copies and pastes the same answers between services.

### Posting is one more task that gets put off

No posts means no comments and no messages. And when you finally post, nobody keeps an eye on what comes in afterwards.

WHAT IT IS

## What are automatic messages on Instagram?

They’re replies your account sends on its own, without anyone on your team writing them. Instagram only offers quick replies, which someone still has to send by hand; Bookline connects through Meta’s official API and answers with AI, using your restaurant’s information.

### Three things it does for you

#### Answers DMs

Bookings, menu, opening hours and location, straight away and in the guest’s language.

casa\_marina

Do you have a terrace?

Yes! A heated terrace all year round. Shall I book you a table outside?

#### Turns comments into DMs

Anyone who comments a keyword on your post gets a private message instantly.

casa\_marina

Commented “MENU” on your post

Here’s our autumn menu! 🍂 Shall I save you a table this weekend?

#### Publishes and schedules

Schedule the post from Bookline and, in the same step, the automatic reply to its comments.

Autumn menu 🍂

Fri · 12:00

![](/_next/image?url=%2Fimages%2Fblog-escandallo-restaurante-costes-rentabilidad.webp&w=3840&q=75)

Comments with “MENU” → automatic DM

24/7

Replies late at night and mid-service, when nobody can check the phone.

Official API

A connection authorised by Meta, without sharing your account password.

Their language

Replies in the language each guest writes in.

USE CASES

## What your guests ask you on Instagram

Every conversation ends where it should: in a booking, on your menu, or with your team when it’s needed.

Book a tableAsk for the menuGiveaways and promotionsThe usual questionsOutside opening hours

### Bookings completed inside the chat

The guest asks for a table and the assistant offers the times left and confirms the booking, without leaving Instagram.

*   Offers the times still available
*   Confirms the booking in the same chat
*   If something gets complicated, hands the conversation to your team

casa\_marina

Hi! Do you have a table for 4 on Saturday at 9 pm?

Hello! Yes, we have room at 9:00 pm and 9:30 pm. Which works best?

9:00 pm

Booked: Saturday, 9:00 pm, 4 people. Your confirmation will arrive here.

### The menu, for whoever asks

They comment MENU on your post or ask for it by DM, and get the link instantly.

*   Replies to comments and to direct messages
*   The link you choose: menu, set lunch, group menu
*   And it offers a table while it’s at it

casa\_marina

Commented “MENU” on your post

Hi! Here’s our autumn menu 🍂 casamarina.com/menu

Thanks! Anything gluten-free?

Yes, the dishes marked GF on the menu. Shall I save you a table?

### Giveaways that don’t eat up your day

Ask people to comment a word to enter and the assistant replies to every entrant in private, with the rules or the next step.

*   One private reply per entrant
*   Whatever keywords you want on each post
*   Everything stays in the log

casa\_marina

Commented “GIVEAWAY” on your post

You’re in! 🎉 We announce the winner in our stories on Friday. In the meantime, fancy booking a table?

### Opening hours, directions and more, without copy and paste

What your team answers ten times a day, answered on its own with your restaurant’s information.

*   Opening hours and closing days
*   How to get there and where to park
*   Vegan, gluten-free or kids’ options

casa\_marina

Are you open on Mondays?

We’re closed on Mondays, but from Tuesday to Sunday we’re open 1–4 pm and 8–11:30 pm!

### Answers at 1 am just like at 3 pm

Messages arrive when nobody can check the phone, many of them from tourists. The assistant answers at any hour and in their language.

*   24/7, no shifts
*   In the guest’s language
*   Handover to your team when needed

casa\_marina

01:12

¡Hola! ¿Tenéis mesa para dos mañana por la noche?

¡Hola! Sí, nos queda a las 20:30 y a las 21:30. ¿Cuál te va mejor?

Comparison

## Instagram quick replies vs. AI-powered automated messages

Quick replies save typing, but someone still has to read every message and send them. Bookline's automated messages reply on their own.

|     | Instagram quick replies | Automated messages with Bookline |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Included free in Instagram | Yes | No  |
| Replies without anyone on the team keeping watch | No  | Yes |
| Understands the question and answers with your restaurant's information | No  | Yes |
| Finds a table and confirms the booking in the chat | No  | Yes |
| Sends a DM to anyone who comments a keyword | No  | Yes |
| Replies in the small hours and mid-service | No  | Yes |
| Replies in the customer's language | No  | Yes |

Quick replies: saved texts in Instagram that your team inserts by hand into each conversation.

HOW IT WORKS

## Up and running in four steps

Connect your account, tell it what it needs to know about your restaurant, and the assistant starts answering.

# What can an Instagram booking assistant actually do?

Learn to assess an Instagram assistant with concrete examples, clear responsibilities and a fallback when a customer request exceeds its permissions.

![A salon professional checks a phone beside an appointment notebook.](/blog/images/instagram-booking-assistant-capabilities.webp)

In this article

*   [Write a small capability card before connecting](https://klioso.app/blog/instagram-booking-assistant-capabilities#heading-1)
*   [Check the real account and the entry points](https://klioso.app/blog/instagram-booking-assistant-capabilities#heading-2)
*   [Set a limit for pictures, voice and missing context](https://klioso.app/blog/instagram-booking-assistant-capabilities#heading-3)
*   [Give answers a source and appointments a separate check](https://klioso.app/blog/instagram-booking-assistant-capabilities#heading-4)
*   [Make unfinished conversations visible](https://klioso.app/blog/instagram-booking-assistant-capabilities#heading-5)
*   [Judge results by category, then expand carefully](https://klioso.app/blog/instagram-booking-assistant-capabilities#heading-6)
*   [Key takeaway](https://klioso.app/blog/instagram-booking-assistant-capabilities#heading-7)

An Instagram booking assistant can help answer routine enquiries and direct clients towards a booking, but its actual scope depends on the account connection, supported message types and permissions. It may have no authority to reserve or change appointments. Evaluate it as a collection of specific tasks rather than a promise to “manage Direct”. The useful question is what happens to each customer request from arrival to a clear outcome, including requests the assistant cannot safely complete.

## Write a small capability card before connecting

Take five recent, anonymised enquiries and describe the result each person needed. “What does a haircut cost?” requires a verified price. “Can you fix this colour?” requires professional assessment. A reaction to a story may contain neither a question nor booking intent. Putting these messages in one automation category hides the different responsibilities involved.

For every task, write down four things:

*   the kind of incoming request;
*   the information or permission needed;
*   the result the assistant may report;
*   the fallback when that result cannot be reached.

For a standard service question, the result might be an accurate explanation followed by the booking page. For a special request, it might be a question passed to you without any promised appointment. Keep this card short enough to discuss with a provider. It becomes a practical acceptance checklist, not a list of impressive features.

Prepare the booking destination

Keep your KLIOSO services and booking page current before directing Instagram enquiries to them.

[Start free ↗](https://app.klioso.app/?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=organic&utm_campaign=instagram_booking_assistant_capabilities&utm_content=en_inline_cta)

## Check the real account and the entry points

An integration must support the Instagram account and connection route you actually use. Meta provides messaging interfaces for professional accounts, but that does not mean every service implements every available route or permission. Ask the provider to identify the account that will be connected and demonstrate incoming messages from an ordinary customer account, not only from its own test account.

Then distinguish the entry points your customers use. A direct text message, a story reply, a shared post and a public comment are different situations. Do not infer that an assistant reads comments because it can answer a direct message. Equally, a profile connection does not prove it can read every part of a conversation.

Keep ownership of access with your business. Know which administrator authorises the connection and where it can be disconnected. You should not need to guess which account a client is actually reaching.

## Set a limit for pictures, voice and missing context

Beauty enquiries often depend on an attachment: a reference hairstyle, a photograph of previous work or a voice message explaining a desired result. A system may receive the message without being able to interpret that attachment. Even when image or audio processing is supported, it does not automatically grant the assistant the professional judgement needed to recommend a treatment.

Test these ordinary cases separately:

*   a question written entirely as text;
*   a photograph with a short caption;
*   a voice message without a written summary;
*   a reference to an earlier post or conversation.

If the relevant content is unavailable, the answer should acknowledge the gap and ask for a useful clarification or pass the request on. “I can help with the listed services; the professional needs to review your reference photo” is more honest than a confident guess. Avoid asking the client to send additional personal material simply to keep the conversation going.

## Give answers a source and appointments a separate check

Routine answers need maintained business information. Price, duration, address and preparation instructions should come from a source you recognise and update. A price mentioned in an old promotion is not necessarily the current price, and a previous conversation is not permission to repeat an exception for a new customer.

Consider someone asking for a haircut at five tomorrow. An information assistant can explain the service and direct them to available times on the booking page. It cannot truthfully say “five is reserved” merely because the wording sounds helpful. If a provider claims calendar actions, ask it to demonstrate the resulting appointment with the right service, person and time.

A useful demonstration includes an unavailable time as well as a successful request. The assistant should explain the limit or offer a valid next step, rather than invent availability. Treat the saved appointment as evidence of the action; treat the message as communication about that evidence.

## Make unfinished conversations visible

Some enquiries will remain unresolved. The important question is where they go and who notices them. A client requesting a person should reach a real review route. A complaint, an unclear request or a failed connection should not disappear behind an endlessly repeated greeting.

Agree on a manageable operating routine:

*   name the person responsible for unresolved requests;
*   choose when that person will review them;
*   preserve the latest question and relevant context;
